listings.name: Santa Maria del Fiore
listings.content: The cathedral interior is to a basilica pattern; it's vast and at first feels dark and empty. Give your eyes time to adjust, and admire the stained glass windows, funeral monument of Bishop d'Orso, and altar of St Zanobius. Below is the Crypt (M-Sa 10:00-17:00) with remains of the preceding cathedral of Santa Reparata, and the tomb of Brunelleschi. Giotto is believed to lie here somewhere, but his tomb has yet to be identified. Above is the soaring cupola or Dome. The cathedral is free, but you need a pre-booked ticket and time-slot to climb the 464 steps up to the Dome (entrance north side of the church). Slots are available M-F 08:30-19:00, Sa 08:30-17:00 and Su 13:00-16:00.

listings.name: Giotto's Tower
listings.content: Almost 85 tall, with 414 steps to climb, this richly decorated tower is topped by an open terrace with a panorama of the Duomo, city and surrounds.

listings.name: Baptistery
listings.content: Octagonal plan, with a pyramidal roof covering its dome. It's famous for its bronze doors by Andrea Pisano (14th century) and Lorenzo Ghiberti (15th century) and a beautiful interior vault decorated with 13th-century mosaics. The interior is being restored and is unviewable as of April 2024, though the exterior can be seen.

listings.name: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo
listings.content: This houses original artworks from the Duomo and surrounding religious buildings, including sculptures by Donatello, a Michelangelo Pietà (different from his version in Saint Peter's, Rome) and the losing entries in the 1401 contest to design the doors of the Baptistery. Plus models and drawings of the Cathedral.

listings.name: Galleria degli Uffizi
listings.content: Outstanding fine art museum with Renaissance paintings and sculptures from classical antiquity. It's in a late 16th-century palazzo designed by Vasari, in two wings enclosing a long narrow courtyard, effectively a street, an innovation in its day. Originally the palazzo was magistrates' offices (hence "Uffizi") and state archives; then it came to house the Medici's vast art collection. However, one collections seems to have crossed purposes: the massive number of standardized portraits, placed in the hallway, seem to have been an ID system for identifying important foreigners when they came to town. The artworks are on the first and second floors, they keep the lifts well hidden. Highlights include Birth of Venus by Boticelli, Dukes of Urbino by della Francesca, Medusa by Caravaggio, Venus of Urbino by Titian, Annunciation by da Vinci, Pope Leo X and family by Raphael, Velasquez' self-portrait, Rembrandt's final self-portrait, and many other big names. Allow three hours for a visit. Uffizi specialises in the Renaissance, so although later styles are represented, examples are few: you don't really come here for the 18th- to 20th-century material. The restaurant/cafè has a large balcony overlooking the main piazza with good views of the Palazzo Vecchio, and naturally their prices reflect the views.
listings.price: High season (21 Feb-9 Nov; 21 Dec-9 Jan): adult €29 (or €23 for early morning tickets: 08:15 and 08:30), conc €6, combi with Pitti & Boboli €38; low season: adult €16, conc €6, combi €18; including a booking fee of €4

listings.name: Bargello
listings.content: Used as a barracks and prison until the 19th century, this museum houses some of the best Renaissance and Mannerist sculpture. Big names here include Michelangelo, Donatello, Ammannati, Bandinelli, Andrea and Jacopo Sansovino, Desiderio da Settignano, Giambologna, and Antonio Rossellino. It also displays ceramics, textiles & tapestries, ivory, silver, armour and coins. Allow two hours. Not nearly as crowded as the Uffizi or Galleria dell'Accademia and paying a fee to book in advance is likely not necessary.
listings.image: Sala del Verrocchio museo nazionale del Bargello Firenze.jpg

listings.name: Galleria dell'Accademia
listings.content: Highlights are Michelangelo's original David (the one in Piazza della Signoria is a copy) and his unfinished Slaves. It also includes Florentine painting, a museum of musical instruments, and Russian icons. No photography is allowed inside. N.B. the "Accademia di Belle Arti" next door is a university department, not connected with the Gallery.

listings.name: Palazzo Pitti
listings.content: The original Pitti was a banker; the palace has housed royalty but became best known for its Medici family treasures. It's now divided into four museums (same ticket): ground floor is the Treasury of the Grand Dukes; first floor houses the Palatine Gallery and the Royal and Imperial Apartments, second floor is the Modern Art Gallery and the Museum of Costume and Fashion. The Boboli gardens are just behind the palazzo.
listings.price: Mar-Oct: adult €16, conc €8, combi with Uffizi & Boboli €38; Nov-Feb: adult €10, conc €5, combi €18; booking fee €4

listings.name: Palazzo Davanzati
listings.content: a house museum with antique fittings and furniture

listings.name: Museo Galileo
listings.content: This museum shows the evolution of the instruments used in various scientific fields such as mathematics, physics, biology, chemistry, astronomy. The room of Galileo Galilei shows some of his original instruments as well as models from his drawings. The room of Spheres and Globes houses an excellent cartographic collection. In a rather macabre twist the museum also has the middle finger of Galileo's right hand on display. The museum offer some descriptions in Italian and English but you can access other languages by scanning QR codes (Chinese, French, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, German). The museum offers an open WiFi. It is recommended to have an idea of the principles behind the instruments (as the descriptions on the labels are rather generic). For that, you can download their free audio-guide app available in Italian and English (Google Play, Apple Store) and get an idea of the instruments displayed.

listings.name: Museo Horne
listings.content: Displays art and furnishings of the 14th & 15th century. The building and art collection were owned by art historian Herbert Percy Horne.
listings.address: Palazzo Corsi on via dei Benci, 6

listings.name: Archaeological Museum
listings.content: The Etruscan art collection is particularly good.

listings.name: Museo Novecento
listings.content: Gallery of 20th- & 21st-century art, on three floors of a palazzo.

listings.name: Museo Marini
listings.content: Houses the work of that contemporary sculptor.

listings.name: Stibbert Museum
listings.content: Has a great collection of armour and arms.

listings.name: Palazzo Vecchio
listings.content: Old city palace/city hall, adorned with fine art. The replica of Michelangelo's "David" is placed outside the main door in the original location of the statue, which is a symbol of the Comune of Florence. The site displays an important collection of Renaissance sculptures and paintings, including the Putto by Verrochio and the series of murals by Giorgio Vasari at the Salone dei Cinquecento (Hall of the Five Hundreds) - the hall which used to display the now lost Renaissance masterpiece, that is, the so-called Battaglia di Anghiari, by Leonardo da Vinci.
listings.price: "Museum" or "Tower and Battlements": €12.50 adults, €10 concessions. "Museum" and "Tower and Battlements": €17.50 adults, €15 concessions
listings.image: Firenze Palazzo della Signoria, better known as the Palazzo Vecchio.jpg

listings.name: Ponte Vecchio
listings.content: The oldest and most celebrated bridge over the Arno, and the only Florentine bridge to survive World War II. The design is distinctive: it's a three-arched bridge supporting a parade of shops supporting another bridge. It dates to 1345 (hence Ponte Vecchio, "old bridge"), with earlier bridges being swept away by floods, rebuilt and swept away again. At street level it's a pedestrianised cobbled arch. It's lined by shops, which were butchers until Renaissance times then - in an insight as dramatic as the discovery of perspective in painting - they realised that goldsmiths' shops paid higher rents and didn't stink; so from then to this day it's just been overpriced jewellery shops and market stalls. Above these is the higher bridge, the Vasari Corridor, a private walkway added in 1565 so that the Medici Dukes could move between Palazzo Vecchio (Town Hall) and Palazzo Pitti (their blingy residence) without mixing with common folk. On the south bank, the Corridor nowadays continues as a gallery of the Uffizi, and there is sometimes talk of extending this over the bridge, or otherwise making the space accessible. Nothing's come of this so far, so the common folk will have to continue admiring the scene from street level.

listings.name: Santa Croce
listings.content: Contains the monumental tombs of Galileo, Michelangelo, Machiavelli, Dante, Rossini, and many other notables in addition to artistic decorations. There is also great artwork in the church. The Museo dell'Opera di Santa Croce (included in ticket) displays a flood-damaged but still beautiful Crucifix by Cimabue (Giotto's teacher), which has become a symbol of the disastrous floods of 1966. The ticket also includes Pazzi Chapel, a perfectly symmetrical example of sublime neo-Classic Renaissance architecture.

listings.name: Santa Maria Novella
listings.content: A beautiful church with great artwork, including a Trinity by Masaccio that is being restored as of April 2024 but can still be seen from the scaffold for an additional charge of €1.50 and a great series of frescoes by Ghirlandaio behind the altar. Also, the museum near the Chiostro Verde, outside the church to its left (follow the signs in the church), contains gently restored frescoes of Old Testament scenes by Paolo Uccello which are quite unusual in style and well worth seeing. Off of another cloister is the wonderful Spanish Chapel which is covered in huge, impressive 14th-century frescoes. Also don't miss the Cappella Strozzi di Mantova, up a flight of stairs at the end of the left transept, with dramatic frescoes of Heaven, Hell and Purgatory by Nardo di Cione. The gift shop is in the Sacristy, which also contains paintings and other artwork. Allotting 1 1/2-2 hours to see everything would be reasonable.

listings.name: Orsanmichele
listings.content: A beautiful old church from the 14th century, which once functioned as a grain market.

listings.name: San Lorenzo
listings.content: The façade of this church was never completed, giving it a striking, rustic appearance. Inside the church is pure Renaissance neo-classical splendor. If you go around the back of the church, there is a separate entrance to the Medici chapels. Be sure to check out the stunning burial chapel of the princes and the sacristy down the corridor. The small sacristy is blessed with the presence of nine Michelangelo sculptures.

listings.name: San Marco Convent
listings.content: Houses frescoes by Fra Angelico and his workshop. Fra Angelico painted a series of frescoes for the cells in which the Dominican monks lived.
listings.image: Firenze, chiesa e convento di san marco, facciata 01.jpg

listings.name: Great Synagogue and Jewish Museum of Florence
listings.content: Lovely Moorish-style synagogue built in 1882 and a museum with many artefacts and documentation of Florentine Jewish life going back many centuries; audio tours in multiple languages are available.
listings.price: €6.50 total for the synagogue and museum

listings.name: The English Cemetery
listings.content: In the 19th century, the "English Cemetery" received anyone that the city's churchyards wouldn't receive, e.g. Orthodox Christians, but Britons and Americans were the majority. Famous names here include Elizabeth Barrett Browning, Fanny Trollope and Beatrice Shakespeare, a relative of William. There are lots of ornate gravestones with flowery inscriptions in multiple languages.

listings.name: Piazza della Signoria
listings.content: Piazza della Signoria is the grand open space in front: not quite a square, as Palazzo Vecchio blocks out one corner. Sights here are the equestrian statue of Cosimo de Medici, the Fountain of Neptune, the statue of David, and Loggia dei Lanzi, an open arched gallery of Renaissance sculpture
listings.image: Giuseppe Zocchi - The Piazza della Signoria in Florence - WGA25992.jpg

listings.name: Santa Felicita
listings.content: Contains frescoes of the Annunciation and a painting of the Deposition of Christ by the brilliant and weird mannerist painter, Pontormo. They are to be found in the Barbadori Chapel, which is to your immediate right when entering the church.

listings.name: Boboli Gardens
listings.content: Elaborately landscaped and with many interesting sculptures, behind the Pitti Palace. Wonderful city views. Don't miss the Bardini gardens. Entrance to that is included in the combination ticket price for the Boboli, and it's a short walk from the Boboli Gardens. There are great views of the Duomo from the Bardini gardens.

listings.name: Santa Maria del Carmine
listings.content: Famous frescoes (Masaccio’s Adam and Eve Banished From the Garden and others by Lippi and Masolino) in the Brancacci Chapel.
listings.image: Piazza del Carmine, veduta sulla chiesa del carmine.jpg

listings.name: Piazzale Michelangelo
listings.content: Plaza on a hillside with a great view of the city. Go there by bus or climb the stairs and paths from the Lungarno della Zecca.

listings.name: San Miniato al Monte
listings.content: The Sacristy contains frescoes by Spinello Aretino. In the cemetery near this church there are graves of famous people of Florence, including Carlo Lorenzi (Collodi) - author of the famous Pinocchio. Also, turn around when you reach the top of the stairs before entering the church, to see perhaps an even greater view of the city than from nearby Piazzale Michelangelo.

listings.name: Enjoy the view from the Piazzale Michelangelo
listings.content: It's a big square on a hill, but somewhat distant from the traditional tourist sites. It's easy to reach it even on foot using the stairs called "Rampe di San Niccolò". They are on the side of the Arno RIver just in front of the national library. Do this during the summer and during the night to admire Florence's lights.

listings.name: Firenze Rafting
listings.content: Guided rafting trips on the Arno through the historic centre, passing beneath Ponte Vecchio. Tours last about one hour, require no previous experience and are run in inflatable rafts with an instructor in each boat. Equipment is provided; participants should expect to get wet. Booking in advance is required.
listings.address: Arno riverbank in front of the Torre San Niccolò

listings.name: Impruneta spa
listings.content: The thermal waters of Impruneta spring from two sources and are used to treat respiratory diseases, liver, gastrointestinal, and skin allergies.

listings.name: Florence Photography Workshop & Tour
listings.content: Discover Florence with your camera and with a professional photography teacher (a Vogue-featured American photographer) and an official Florence guide at your side.

listings.name: ABC School
listings.content: Italian language school offering language and cultural courses since 1982.

listings.name: Centro Machiavelli
listings.content: Italian language and cultural school for foreigners. The structure and the contents of the programmes for the levels are based on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. The school also organises a programme of cultural activities and excursions to complement the language classes and enable the students to come into contact with the Italian culture and practice Italian in the field.

listings.name: Istituto Galilei
listings.content: Italian language school specializing in one-to-one, personalized and small group (max 4 people) full immersion courses.

listings.name: Michelangelo Institute
listings.content: Italian study programmes for foreign students. Cooking workshop, art history classes, plastic arts and visual arts programs are also taught in this academy.

listings.name: Scuola Leonardo da Vinci Florence
listings.content: Offers a wide choice of Italian language and culture courses for children and adults from beginning to advanced levels.

listings.name: Cooking Class
listings.content: Florence and Tuscany are becoming synonymous with "cooking class". Tuscan cuisine is appreciated worldwide and a cooking class experience is now more and more part of the attraction of Tuscany, as a way of carrying back home memories and improved cooking skills. There are many in the area, either in historical villas in the countryside or in central Florence, from Florentine use of tripe and giblets to the use of organic ingredients from the local producers, and classes range widely in size. During high season, make sure to book in advance.

listings.name: I fratellini
listings.content: Good street food: panini for €5 (Mar 2024) and wine for €2+ (Oct 2018) from a tiny hole in the wall. Patrons eat on the sidewalk while resting their glass of wine on small shelves nested along the street wall.

listings.name: Trattoria Mario
listings.content: Lunch only, no booking, you'll be seated with other walk-ins. Good food, try to save room for a meat main course.

listings.name: Trattoria Le Mossacce
listings.content: Reliable local eatery. Local produce and meats are prepared simply using traditional recipes and time-honoured tradition. Some pastas are made fresh daily, so ask for the daily special. If you want to experience Bistecca alla Fiorentina (Florentine-style steak), they do it amazingly without breaking your wallet. They sell and cut the steak from a larger rib slab in increments of 100g (with a minimum of 500g per serving).

listings.name: Self-Service Ristorante Leonardo
listings.content: Although there is a menu at the entrance, it is better to go straight in and pick what you like. You can also order Bistecca alla Fiorentina.
listings.price: Primi €3.5-4. Secondi €4.5-5.5. About €10 per person for a full-course dinner (Oct 2018)

listings.name: Tiona Asian Restaurant
listings.content: Not that you'd admit to wanting a break from Italian food, but this small friendly Sri Lankan restaurant makes a refreshing change. Ayubowan!

listings.name: Pescheria Sugarello
listings.content: Seafood. Excellent fried calamari and grilled fish fillet with vegetables. You can find also fresh oysters. Be there early, as it gets packed very easily.

listings.name: Amici di Ponte Vecchio
listings.content: Pizza, schiacciata, homemade sandwiches, wine by the glass, takeaway.

listings.name: Il Vegetariano
listings.content: Budget restaurant with more formal front room, the eclectic middle room, or the peaceful outdoor garden in the back. Daily changing menu with vegan and gluten-free items clearly marked, desserts, salads, soups, hearty brown bread, and a good selection of coffee, tea, wine, beer, and liqueur.

listings.name: Trattoria Zà Zà
listings.content: A very nicely decorated restaurant with many vegetarian choices. You can choose to sit inside or outside in the piazza. The menu is huge, lots of choices, and the prices are fair. Service is outstanding, they really cater to your needs. Make sure to try the chianti house wine. Note that they have two seating areas on the piazza: between are two other restaurants, Cantastorie and Garibaldi.

listings.name: al Tranvai
listings.content: Tourists seldom venture this far south. Traditional Tuscan food at decent prices. 1st courses at €7, mains at €10 to €16 and vino at €4 / 0.5L (Oct 2018). The rabbit, asparagus souffle and fiori fritti are excellent and the service very welcoming and warm.

listings.name: "Il Latini" Restaurant
listings.content: Fun place, communal seating and lively staff. The steaks are good.

listings.name: Trattoria Palle D'Oro dal 1860
listings.content: Long-standing family-run Tuscan restaurant. This is where the locals come, not least for the low prices. Fixed price 2-course lunch or €13, dinner €14 (Oct 2018)

listings.name: Trattoria Cammillo
listings.content: Fairly good Tuscan cuisine, with a number of options for vegetarians and vegans. Make reservations or be there as they open.

listings.name: Enoteca Pinchiorri
listings.content: Michelin-starred restaurant with exquisite meals at splurge prices.

listings.name: B-Roof
listings.content: Fine dining with wonderful night panorama of the city.

listings.name: Il Cibreo
listings.content: Great choice of Tuscan food, with highly selected ingredients.

listings.name: Trattoria da Tito
listings.content: Although a bit of a walk from the main attractions, this restaurant speaks for itself with mandatory reservations. Great Italian food and atmosphere. Dinner often includes impromptu free drinks and lively table staff.

listings.name: Gelateria dei Neri
listings.content: Ice cream in many flavors, some experimental, all excellent.

listings.name: Festival Del Gelato
listings.content: 50 flavors and has an upbeat atmosphere

listings.name: Vivoli
listings.content: Via Isole delle Stinche, 7/R. Close to Piazza Santa Croce. Vivoli has a good gelato fruit selection, so definitely try the fragola, or strawberry. Make sure that you ask for the cream on top as well, because it adds another element to an already great dessert.

listings.name: La Cite
listings.content: A very nice and cozy cafe/bookstore. Good prices, nice atmosphere, good books. Borgo San Frediano 20r.

listings.name: Enoteca Le volpi e l'Uva
listings.content: The must of the tasting wines and savory titbits. Piazza dei Rossi, 1.

listings.name: Été
listings.content: A lovely little café with warm service and good local beer and wine.

listings.name: Cavalli Club
listings.content: Roberto Cavalli, Italian fashion designer, has one his beautiful clubs in Florence. The inside has a stage with a projector of Roberto Cavalli's fashion shows running non-stop. The upstairs can be a private lounge for parties or VIP section on certain nights. This club was the most popular on Wednesday nights, but it’s open on the weekends as well. It’s black and leopard interior fits the natural and animalistic designs Roberto Cavalli creates. Roberto and his two sons are frequently at the club so look out! All ages are appropriate and the dress attire here is rather upscale. This is not just a seasonal club so all year visitors are encouraged to go.

listings.name: Bamboo Lounge Club
listings.content: Bamboo Lounge Club is a great place for young adults and students to party. The music is great from European to American techno and many other worldwide DJs. Bamboo Lounge Club offers VIP tables and has two midsized bars. It is very clean and safe to be in. It is located on Via Giuseppe Verdi not far from the Duomo. Dress is a little more than casual, but not too upscale. The loud music, dancing, and exciting atmosphere gives people a chance to let loose and have fun. The club features mostly house, techno and hip hop music.

listings.name: Tenax
listings.content: If you love house and electronic music this is the best club to go to. It’s a two-story club, located on the outskirts of Florence, features DJ’s from all around Europe, America, and Australia. This club also holds many concerts during the winter and summer. Many people come from all over to enjoy this club's atmosphere. The dance floor is extremely large and is always very crowded. Be smart where you keep your bag and wallet because it’s very easy to get pick pocketed in large clubs like this. This club usually has a cover of €20 and the drinks are rather expensive, but it is a great place to experience at least once. It is very different than most of the clubs in Florence because of the multi-story building. To venture here would be best by taxi or bus. Since it is located in the outskirts of Florence walking could be difficult and not advised. There are many people who can help in directions in the Santa Maria Novella Station.

listings.name: Hostel Florence Experience
listings.content: A hostel in a historic Florentine noble palace built in the 14th century and modified in the 17th century. Rooms are occasionally clean.

listings.name: Hostel Archi Rossi
listings.content: Never mind the renaissance-kitsch walls. Rooms are clean and rates include breakfast, dinner (except Saturdays) and internet access.

listings.name: Hostel 7 Santi
listings.content: A converted 19th-century convent. Rooms are clean and quiet. Has dorm bunks and private rooms.

listings.name: B&B Duomo View
listings.content: Large choice of double bedrooms. Services are in common and some of the guestrooms boast a fantastic view of the Duomo. Internet connection and breakfast also available.

listings.name: B&B Giglio Bianco
listings.content: This B&B has just the one room, the Camera Verde. They feature gourmet meals and cooking classes directed by Chef Vary.

listings.name: B&B di Piazza del Duomo
listings.content: A small B&B, rooms with private bathroom and shower, A/C, LCD TV, free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: B&B Tourist House Battistero
listings.content: A lovely B&B in the centre, with the Duomo just 30 m away.

listings.name: Florence Stadium B&B
listings.content: 3-star with clean, spacious rooms near the Stadium and Mandela Forum.

listings.name: Giulia Residence
listings.content: Decent 3-star, access through clanky iron gate in apartment block.

listings.name: Opera Boutique B&B
listings.content: Historic building of the late nineteenth century.

listings.name: Arizona Hotel
listings.content: This 3-star hotel is in a renovated villa from the 18th century.

listings.name: Convitto della Calza
listings.content: 3 star in converted 16th-century cloister, with frescoed rooms and a modern conference centre.

listings.name: Hotel Desirèe
listings.content: Friendly 3-star with 18 rooms, next to railway station.

listings.name: Hotel Byron
listings.content: Three-star hotel with parking.

listings.name: Hotel Casci
listings.content: This small 2-star is in a 15th-century palace and has some original fresco ceilings. Composer Gioacchino Rossini lived here in the 19th century.

listings.name: Hotel Dali
listings.content: One star, consistently clean & cosy, good location, owners Marco and Samanta helpful and fluent in English.

listings.name: Hotel Fiorita
listings.content: Next to railway station, on 3rd floor of building that has two other hotels. Rooms have a/c, TV and a safety deposit box. Some rooms also have modem sockets.

listings.name: Hotel Masaccio
listings.content: Cozy one-star in a 20th-century villa, with restaurant.

listings.name: Hotel Giglio
listings.content: Simple 3-star on edge of centro storico.

listings.name: Hotel Kursaal & Ausonia
listings.content: A small 2-star, basic but clean.

listings.name: Hotel Lorena
listings.content: Two-star hotel in the historic centre, simple but comfy.

listings.name: Hotel Montreal
listings.content: Two star, central but basic and dated.

listings.name: Hotel Palazzuolo
listings.content: Basic 2-star, many stairs & no lift, but central.

listings.name: Hotel Romagna
listings.content: Two-star hotel near SMN train station. 22 bedrooms en suite, internet connection and satellite TV. Cosy (ie small rooms, basic), no lift to upper floors.

listings.name: Hotel Delle Tele
listings.content: Central 3-star near SMN Duomo.

listings.name: Albergo Firenze
listings.content: 2-star hotel, central but basic.

listings.name: Il Bargello B&B
listings.content: Clean friendly 3-star.

listings.name: FH Calzaiuoli Hotel
listings.content: Central 4-star going on 3.

listings.name: Hotel Caravaggio
listings.content: Good 3-star, consistently clean, well-run & helpful.

listings.name: Galileo Hotel
listings.content: 3 star in an elegant 19th-century building, but a/c and wifi erratic.

listings.name: Hotel Basilea Florence
listings.content: This 3-star hotel offers 38 bedrooms, single, double, twin, triple and 2 large suites, all with private bath, television and internet connection.

listings.name: Hotel Boston
listings.content: 3-star hotel with 16 bedrooms, not all en-suite. Clean but small and basic.

listings.name: Hotel Crocini
listings.content: Central 2-star, not all rooms en suite.

listings.name: Hotel La Gioconda
listings.content: 3-star hotel.

listings.name: Hotel Il Guelfo Bianco
listings.content: 3-star in a 15th-century building.

listings.name: Hotel Malaspina
listings.content: 3-star in charming a late 19th-century residence, enriched with modern comforts.

listings.name: Hotel Marignolle
listings.content: 4-star in hills outside town, in bosky Tuscan scenery. Outdoor pool May to October.
listings.address: Via di San Quirichino a Marignolle 16

listings.name: Hotel Mario's
listings.content: Central 3-star.

listings.name: Hotel Mia Cara
listings.content: Small 3-star a short walk from Santa Maria Novella. Friendly English-speaking staff.

listings.name: Hotel Morandi alla Crocetta
listings.content: Comfy 3-star in a Dominican 16th-century convent. On-site garage parking is available.

listings.name: Privilege Hotel
listings.content: 3-star hotel on the bank of the Arno, with single, double, triple and "Family" rooms. Breakfast buffet, hotel bar and garage available.

listings.name: Relais Villa Antea
listings.content: Historical residence in an old palazzo with friendly staff. Rooms are spacious.

listings.name: Hotel Rivoli
listings.content: 4-star in a former 14th-century Franciscan convent.

listings.name: Hotel De Rose Palace
listings.content: 4-star hotel in a traditional Florentine mansion.

listings.name: Hotel Savonarola
listings.content: 3-star with one single and 15 twin, double, triple and quadruple rooms. All with private bath, Wi-Fi connection, telephone and breakfast included.

listings.name: Novotel Firenze Nord Aeroporto
listings.content: 4-star handy for airport. Well out of city but they have free shuttle to the city center.

listings.name: Villa il Mosaico
listings.content: Elegant villa, ten self-catering apartments with kitchen, living room, bathroom, internet connection and TV. Private parking and 100 square metre terrace with solarium.

listings.name: Residence Select Executive
listings.content: 4-star hotel; 12 rooms, some with kitchenette.

listings.name: Hotel Unicorno
listings.content: Small 3-star hotel in a 17th-century building.

listings.name: Grand Hotel Adriatico
listings.content: Modern 4-star hotel in the historical centre, very close to the train station. Rooms and suites are suitable for couples, families, single travellers and group of friends. The hotel features a Tuscan restaurant, a private car park, complimentary breakfast served on a terrace on the ground floor and free minibar for direct bookings.

listings.name: Grand Hotel Cavour
listings.content: Friendly, efficient hotel in a 13th-century palazzo. Former residence of the Strozzi-Ridolfi dynasty.

listings.name: J and J Hotel
listings.content: 4-star hotel in former convent. Has double, twin, junior suite, suite, and double rooms for single use, all en-suite services.

listings.name: Kraft Hotel
listings.content: 4-star hotel near the centre with swimming-pool, restaurant and 5th-floor terrace with bar.

listings.name: Hotel Laurus al Duomo
listings.content: A historic 4-star hotel, close to the Cathedral and Firenze SMN railway station.

listings.name: Milu Hotel
listings.content: Central 4-star with roof garden with a charming view.

listings.name: Hotel Mirage
listings.content: Comfortable straightforward 4-star hotel with restaurant. Regard this as an airport hotel and you won't be disappointed.
listings.price: Single from €110, doubles from €140, triples from €160, apartments from €300 per week

listings.name: Hotel Monna Lisa Florence
listings.content: Four-star hotel, and yes it's Monna, that's not a typo. In a restored 14th-century Florentine noble palace. Gym facilities, sun terrace and meeting rooms.

listings.name: Hotel Ponte Vecchio Suites & Spa
listings.content: 4-star hotel with modern rooms and suites. The hotel offers a private spa for two with a hot tub. Continental breakfast and free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: NH Porta Rossa
listings.content: Gorgeous hotel built in the 12th century.

listings.name: L'Orologia
listings.content: Swanky boutique 4-star hotel with rooms themed on watches. Nice view of Piazza & Basilica from breakfast room.

listings.name: Orto de' Medici
listings.content: 4-star hotel in a 19th-century building with gardens.

listings.name: Palazzo Magnani Feroni
listings.content: It's in a 16th-century building that belonged to Marquis Feroni. It has twelve comfortable suites with classic furniture and original frescoes.

listings.name: Residence La Repubblica Florence
listings.content: 21 self-catering apartments for a maximum of six people, all with kitchenette, private bath, internet connection, satellite TV and cooking facilities. Short stays (eg single night) welcome.

listings.name: Hotel Pitti Palace al Ponte Vecchio
listings.content: 4-star overlooking the bridge; you're paying for the location.

listings.name: Villa Poggio ai Merli
listings.content: A historic residence on edge of city, in large park.

listings.name: Villa la Vedetta
listings.content: 5-star luxury hotel with panorama of Florence's skyline.

listings.name: Hotel degli Orafi
listings.content: Boutique 4-star in Florence city centre, overlooking river near Ponte Vecchio.

listings.name: Palazzo Vecchietti
listings.content: Historic residence a few steps from Piazza della Repubblica, in the centre of Florence. Few suites, elegant and modern. The hotel also offers two apartments in the central area. Gluten-free products and breakfast included in the room rate.
listings.image: Via de' Vecchietti 2 angolo via degli Strozzi 4, palazzo vecchietti, 01,0.jpg

listings.name: DoubleTree by Hilton Florence Metropole
listings.content: A 4-star hotel with views of the city. A spa, fitness centre, room service and business centre are available on site.
listings.price: from €80 for a King Guest Room to €150 for a suite

listings.name: Ad Astra Florence
listings.content: A historic residence with 14 rooms enriched by frescoed ceilings and individually furnished with elegant vintage, classic and contemporary touches. The most prestigious rooms and the living room are surrounded by a terrace overlooking the Torrigiani Garden.

listings.name: Palazzo Firenze by Baglioni Hotels & Resorts
listings.content: 5-star hotel in Florence’s historic Santa Croce district, set in an elegant 18th-century palazzo. Offers classic Florentine-style rooms with high ceilings, marble bathrooms, and parquet floors. Refined and quiet, with gourmet dining and easy access to major landmarks (meals not included).
